tomas.texto: Your brain has too many windows open.
tomas.estilo: intriguing and self-assured, like revealing something

tomas.texto: You hunt for a tab. You aim. You drag. You switch desktops blind.
tomas.estilo: listing with rhythm, a little overwhelmed

tomas.texto: And when you finally find it... what were you going to do?
tomas.estilo: with a pause, then knowing confusion

tomas.texto: Every search is a tiny decision. And hundreds of tiny decisions drain your mind.
What if your hand knew the way on its own?
tomas.estilo: excited, slowing down, posing a big idea

tomas.texto: Your brain remembers places better than lists. So give it a map.
tomas.estilo: confident and clear, like a good teacher

tomas.texto: One desktop for each thing. Your thumb goes forward... your thumb goes back.
Rest the pointer on a zone, one tap of your thumb, and its windows rotate. No click.
And tabs switch the same way: without aiming at any of them.
You stop thinking about where everything is. And start thinking about what you're doing.
Now your head has just one window open: the one that matters.
tomas.estilo: warm and unhurried, closing with a smile
